newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's Samir refinery resumes trading.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's Samir refinery resumes trading.

text.p: Samir, Morocco's main oil refinery, which was recently privatised, resumed its trading on Friday at 326.50 dirhams, up 9.5 dirhams compared with last week trading, a bourse official said.

The Moroccan government ceded earlier this week its stake of 67.7 percent in Samir firm to the Swedish-based Saudi Corral Petroleum Holding AB, at 3.5 billion dirhams, or the equivalent of 251 dirhams per share.
"The recent setting up of hard core investors pushed up Samir's shares price....But it might register a correction soon," a Casablanca-based stockbroker said.
Bourse officials suspended Samir's stock trading prior to its privatisation and to stop speculations on the firm's stock, a market analyst said.

Located in a 200 hectares (500 acre) site in Mohammedia on the Atlantic coast, near the industrial and financial centre of Casablanca, the Societe Maroccaine de l'Industrie de Raffinage has a capacity of 6.25 million tonnes per year or 80 percent of Morocco's refined oil products needs.
Among the market's blue-chip firms, Samir has a market capitalisation of around 7.0 billion dirhams while SCP has 1.0 billion dirhams, a broker said.
The firm's turnover grew by 8.6 percent compared with the previous year in spite of a drop in sales volume, the broker said.

Samir has a capital of 1.032 billion dirhams, divided into 20.64 million shares of a 50 dirhams nominal value each. The government floated 30 percent of Samir's capital on the Casablanca stock exchange at $310 million in March 1996.

The government also sold off in the same time its 73.9 percent stake in Societe Cherifienne des Petroles, Morocco's second oil refinery, to Corral group at 473 million dirhams, or the equivalent of 365 dirhams per share.
SCP refinery was not traded on Friday, officials said.
